title: Deep Generative Model in Machine Learning: Theory, Principle and Efficacy
Diffusion Meets Flow Matching
summary: Flow matching and diffusion models are two popular frameworks in generative modeling. Despite seeming similar, there is some confusion in the community about their exact connection. In this post, we aim to clear up this confusion and show that diffusion models and Gaussian flow matching are the same , although different model specifications can lead to different network outputs and sampling schedules. This is great news, it means you can use the two frameworks interchangeably.

title: Valentin De Bortoli (@ValentinDeBort1) — thread (7 tweets)
clean_title: Simplex Diffusion Models carry uncertainty through denoising steps
summary:
[1/7] 🔥Welcome 🔺Simplex Diffusion Models🔻!
Standard discrete diffusion models suffer from "information collapse" because they discard uncertainty at intermediate steps by sampling categorical tokens. (1/5)
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HTYT8EZaMAIlW34.jpg
────────
[2/7] This is usually fixed by considering self-conditioning heuristics but can we do better? We fix this by carrying beliefs across denoising steps and working directly on the probability simplex 🔺.
To do so we introduce 💫 Simplex Diffusion Models 💫(SDMs)
(2/5)
────────
[3/7] SDMs use a Dirichlet forward process where the mean and concentration are set separately. This admits probability paths with closed-form reverse transitions with a DDIM-like rule:
* no ODE integration
* natural extension of the churn parameter to simplex
(3/5)
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HTYTxOpbcAArFAV.jpg
────────
[4/7] Thanks a lot to the amazing @jdeschena (thanks @caglarml for letting us steal him for a few months) @agalashov @AndrewC_ML @liwenliang @JamesTThorn @ArnaudDoucet1! It was a ton of fun working with this elite team 😻
📜 Paper:
(5/5)
────────
[5/7] 🚀 Results: on TinyGSM even without Self-Conditioning (SC), SDMs outperform masked and uniform diffusion! Accuracy hits 49.0% vs 45.8% (MDM + SC) at T=0.1. We also evaluate our model on OWT (and push the Pareto frontier for all baselines there) and GenMol.
(4/5)
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HTYTjOabEAA9Bh4.png
────────
[6/7] (and thanks @nadjushenka_ for the super nice visuals 😻)
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HTYZIAFaQAA52X9.jpg
────────
[7/7] Tagging people who might be interested @sitanch @msalbergo @nmboffi @HannesStaerk @yjelid @LucaAmb @njwfish @json_yim @MoleiTaoMath @_sophia_tang_ @PatrickPyn35903 @k_neklyudov @samsongvch @FrancoisRozet @ssahoo_ @zhihanyang_ @ShamKakade6 @Jaeyeon_Kim_0
clean_summary:
Discrete diffusion models usually lose information during intermediate steps because they sample categorical tokens, which discards uncertainty. This causes "information collapse" and is often fixed with heuristics like self-conditioning.

Valentin De Bortoli and team propose Simplex Diffusion Models (SDMs) that keep beliefs as probabilities on the simplex throughout denoising. They use a Dirichlet forward process with separate mean and concentration, allowing closed-form reverse transitions without ODE integration. On TinyGSM, SDMs outperform previous methods even without self-conditioning, improving accuracy from 45.8% to 49.0% at T=0.1 and advancing results on other benchmarks.

summary:
DMD2 is amazing and used everywhere. But it is very expensive to use in large scale as it requires four models — student, teacher, critic, and the discriminator. DMAD makes DMD much more scalable by using only a student and several lightweight heads through our unification insight of distribution matching and GAN. Check our DMAD! It is fully opensourced! With more powerful tools coming, I can’t wait to see what people with great ideas bring to life—from short films to 4K HDR movies. (Yes, sneaking in another plug for our DiffHDR work here 😉)
Want to try being a director yourself? Try our DMAD!
Huge thanks to the whole team for making DMAD possible! 🙌

🎬 https://pbs.twimg.com/amplify_video_thumb/2106131630402215936/img/FxpZIXMGP4gbhN-D.jpg | https://video-s.twimg.com/amplify_video/2106131630402215936/vid/avc1/472x270/niRqkqbzJ3IWBu4m.mp4?tag=29
clean_summary:
DMD2 is a popular method for video generation, but it needs four models—a student, teacher, critic, and discriminator—which makes it expensive at large scale. Valentin De Bortoli highlights DMAD, which simplifies this by using only a student model with several lightweight heads, based on a new insight that unifies distribution matching and GAN techniques.

DMAD can generate video clips in just four sampling steps and is fully open source. Proof Yu used DMAD to create a trailer by writing the story with GPT-6 and generating every shot with DMAD, showing how it enables faster and more accessible video generation. The project includes code, a paper, and demos for anyone interested in trying it out.

title: Valentin De Bortoli (@ValentinDeBort1)
clean_title: Precision issues in backward passes affect training stability
summary:
Do you really need QKNorm to stablize your training?
Does your "failed training" really failed by bad design?
The answer may lie in your kernel!
We found cudnn, FA4, flex attn ALL have severe precision issue in backward!
And we bring a better kernel here:
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HTuVyVjbMAAtg9Z.jpg
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HTuVyiPbkAAIR9h.jpg
clean_summary:
Valentin De Bortoli points out that training failures might not come from model design or normalization methods like QKNorm, but from precision problems in the kernels used during backpropagation. He found that popular kernels like cudnn, FA4, and flex attention have severe precision issues in their backward computations.

To address this, he shares a better kernel implementation on GitHub that aims to improve numerical stability during training, which could help avoid failures caused by these precision errors.

summary:
💫 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models
Presenting Sigma, the first large-scale (3B/8B) continuous diffusion LM (dLM) trained with likelihood.
📈 Comparable with discrete dLMs and AR on math and coding
🎛️ Enables meaningful study of inference-time interventions
Jointly led with Wei Guo (@WeiGuo01), Jean-Marie Lemercier (@jm_lemercier), Simon Welker (@_cobalamin)
Team: @YongganFu @mmkamani7 Sajad Norouzi @julberner @tomasgeffner @karsten_kreis @YongxinChen1 @MoleiTaoMath @jwthickstun @PavloMolchanov Ante Jukic @ArashVahdat @MardaniMorteza
🎬 https://pbs.twimg.com/amplify_video_thumb/2106926876472348673/img/Z_OGlpuigEbGSP7Z.jpg | https://video-s.twimg.com/amplify_video/2106926876472348673/vid/avc1/480x270/G4YVLRnvRTalcut-.mp4?tag=29
clean_summary:
Valentin De Bortoli presents Sigma, the first large-scale continuous diffusion language model with 3B and 8B parameters trained using likelihood. Unlike discrete diffusion models, Sigma works continuously and matches the performance of discrete diffusion and autoregressive models on math and coding tasks.

This approach also allows researchers to study inference-time interventions more meaningfully. The project is a collaboration involving Wei Guo, Jean-Marie Lemercier, Simon Welker, and a larger team.
